inputs.original_text: Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan is rejecting those allegations of Rs 700 crore corruption tied to the Cooperative Department’s proposed common software project and insists the claims are politically driven. This is the standard leftist dodge we see whenever these politicians get caught pushing big-government schemes that expand state control and drain public resources. Rather than defend traditional family businesses and personal responsibility, they hide behind talk of challenging "entrenched power" while building up collectivist institutions that undermine cultural continuity and national values. We should focus on holding leaders accountable for waste and graft instead of letting them smear critics to protect their ideological experiments that weaken social order.
inputs.modified_text: Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan is trying to wave away the Rs 700 crore corruption allegations connected to the Cooperative Department’s proposed common software project by claiming they're just politically motivated attacks. This is the usual leftist tactic when these politicians are found pushing expansive government projects that grow state power and waste our hard-earned resources. Rather than standing up for traditional family values and individual responsibility, they use excuses about fighting "entrenched power" to justify building up collectivist systems that chip away at our cultural heritage and national identity. We need to demand real accountability for this kind of corruption and inefficiency instead of letting them silence critics to protect their dangerous experiments that erode the social order.
